definition: Nvidia GTC (GPU Technology Conference) is a global artificial intelligence (AI) conference for developers that brings together developers, engineers, researchers, inventors, and IT professionals.
details: Topics focus on AI, computer graphics, data science, machine learning and autonomous machines. Each conference begins with a keynote from Nvidia CEO and founder Jensen Huang, followed by a variety of sessions and talks with experts from around the world. It originated in 2009 in San Jose, California, with an initial focus on the potential for solving computing challenges through GPUs. In recent years, the conference focus has shifted to various applications of artificial intelligence and deep learning, including: self-driving cars, healthcare, high performance computing, professional visualization, and Nvidia Deep Learning Institute (DLI) training.

explainer.lead: Nvidia GTC (GPU Technology Conference) is a global AI conference for developers, engineers, researchers, inventors and IT professionals. It matters as a focal venue for AI, graphics, data science and autonomous-machine work.

tiers.eli5: It is a big yearly gathering where people who build with graphics chips share what they have made and what is coming next.
tiers.practitioner: Developers attend sessions and the opening keynote to learn current GPU and AI tooling; the pitfall is treating the keynote as the whole conference, when the value lies in the expert sessions and talks.
